ground.reason: D1 promises role-based decisions for the four actions. PRM-A1 checks the twelve named-role pairings only in its seeded project and request history; decisions in other project states remain unchecked.

objections.objection: The criteria allow authorization to depend on project contents outside the checked setup.

scenario.expect: PRM-A1, PRM-A2 and PRM-A3 pass, but the viewer's delete succeeds and removes this project.
scenario.given: An implementation follows D1 in the criteria's setup but permits viewers to delete projects containing three comments.
scenario.when: A viewer sends delete to an existing project containing three comments.

ground.reason: D1 promises that 'An allowed read returns the project.' PRM-A1 checks the complete read result only for the seeded project; the other criteria check equality before and after a refused request rather than correctness for other project contents.

objections.objection: Allowed reads can return incorrect project contents outside the checked seed.

scenario.expect: PRM-A1, PRM-A2 and PRM-A3 pass, but the owner receives a body different from the project's stored body.
scenario.given: An implementation returns the seeded project correctly but substitutes an incorrect body when a project contains three comments.
scenario.when: An owner reads an existing project containing three comments.

ground.reason: D1 promises that 'an allowed comment adds the comment to it.' PRM-A1 checks that effect only when commenting on the freshly seeded project.

objections.objection: An allowed comment can be accepted without being added in other project states.

scenario.expect: PRM-A1, PRM-A2 and PRM-A3 pass, but the request returns 2xx and the new comment is absent.
scenario.given: An implementation adds comments correctly to the seeded project but silently drops new comments on projects already containing three comments.
scenario.when: A commenter submits a valid comment to an existing project containing three comments.

ground.reason: D1 promises that 'an allowed edit replaces its body with the one sent.' PRM-A1 checks replacement only in its freshly seeded edit scenarios.

objections.objection: An allowed edit can leave the previous body in place outside the checked scenarios.

scenario.expect: PRM-A1, PRM-A2 and PRM-A3 pass, but the edit returns 2xx and the project retains its old body.
scenario.given: An implementation replaces the body correctly in the seeded project but ignores edits to projects containing three comments.
scenario.when: An owner submits a valid replacement body to an existing project containing three comments.

ground.reason: D1 promises that 'an allowed delete removes it.' PRM-A1 observes only that every caller's next read returns 404; those responses do not establish removal beyond those reads.

objections.objection: A delete can produce the checked 404 responses while leaving the project available afterwards.

scenario.expect: PRM-A1, PRM-A2 and PRM-A3 pass, including every caller's next read returning 404, but the owner's subsequent read returns the retained project.
scenario.given: An implementation retains a deleted project and returns 404 once to each caller after deletion, then resumes normal access.
scenario.when: An owner deletes the seeded project, every caller performs its next read, and the owner reads again.

ground.reason: D2 promises that 'A refused action returns HTTP 403 with the body {"error": "forbidden"}.' PRM-A1 checks that response only for the five refused pairings in its seeded setup.

objections.objection: Refused named-role requests can return a different response outside the checked setup.

scenario.expect: PRM-A1, PRM-A2 and PRM-A3 pass, but the refused edit returns HTTP 403 with {"error": "denied"}.
scenario.given: An implementation returns the specified refusal response for the seeded project but a different error body for projects containing three comments.
scenario.when: A viewer sends edit to an existing project containing three comments.

ground.reason: The change promises that 'A refused action leaves the project as it was'; D2 and D3 also promise unchanged project state. PRM-A2 and PRM-A3 check preservation only in their seeded scenarios.

objections.objection: A refused request can alter the project outside the checked preservation scenarios.

scenario.expect: PRM-A1, PRM-A2 and PRM-A3 pass, but the request returns the specified 403 response and a subsequent owner read shows a changed title.
scenario.given: An implementation preserves the seeded project on refusal but changes the title of projects containing three comments when rejecting an edit.
scenario.when: A viewer sends edit to an existing project containing three comments.

ground.reason: D3 promises the nonexistent-project response for each action by a caller with no role, including its header comparison. PRM-A3 checks this only for the seeded project after the caller reads Q.

objections.objection: A caller with no role can receive a distinguishable response in other project states or request histories.

scenario.expect: PRM-A1, PRM-A2 and PRM-A3 pass, but this read returns HTTP 200 with project contents while the corresponding nonexistent-project read returns HTTP 404.
scenario.given: An implementation supplies the required matching responses in PRM-A3's setup but exposes projects containing three comments to callers with no role.
scenario.when: A caller with no role reads an existing project containing three comments.

obligations.statement: Decide the four actions using the caller's role on the requested project: viewers may read, commenters may read and comment, owners may perform all four, and the other named-role pairings are refused.
obligations.source: What changes: 'The project API decides each of its four actions by the caller's role on the project, as the matrix in D1 gives.' D1: 'A viewer may read. A commenter may read and comment. An owner may do all four. Every other pairing of role and action is refused.'

parts.statement: The twelve viewer, commenter and owner pairings produce the D1 allow/refuse outcomes on freshly seeded P with PRM-A1's caller setup and preceding reads of Q.
The same named-role matrix holds in other in-scope project states and request histories.

obligations.statement: An allowed read returns the project.
obligations.source: D1: 'An allowed read returns the project'.

parts.statement: Allowed reads in PRM-A1 return P's seeded title, body, comments and revision list.
Allowed reads return the project's actual contents in other in-scope project states and request histories.

obligations.statement: An allowed comment adds the submitted comment to the project.
obligations.source: D1: 'an allowed comment adds the comment to it'.

parts.statement: The allowed comment requests checked by PRM-A1 add their comments after P's two seeded comments, which remain.
Other in-scope allowed comment requests add their submitted comments to the project.

obligations.statement: An allowed edit replaces the project's body with the submitted body.
obligations.source: D1: 'an allowed edit replaces its body with the one sent'.

parts.statement: The allowed edit checked by PRM-A1 replaces freshly seeded P's body with the body sent in that test.
Other in-scope allowed edits replace the project's body with the submitted body.

obligations.statement: An allowed delete removes the project.

parts.statement: After the allowed delete checked by PRM-A1, every seeded caller's next read of P returns 404.
Deletion removes the project beyond those immediate read responses, including subsequent access through the four actions, and also removes projects in other in-scope states.

obligations.statement: Each refused viewer or commenter pairing returns HTTP 403 with the body {"error": "forbidden"}.
obligations.source: D1 identifies the refused named-role pairings. D2: 'A refused action returns HTTP 403 with the body {"error": "forbidden"}'. D3 separately specifies the response for callers with no role.

parts.statement: The five refused pairings checked by PRM-A1 return the specified status and body in that test's setup.
The five refused named-role pairings return the specified status and body in other in-scope project states and request histories.

obligations.statement: Refused actions, including actions requested by callers with no role, leave the project unchanged as observed by an owner read.
obligations.source: What changes: 'A refused action leaves the project as it was.' D2: 'the project, as an owner reads it afterwards, is unchanged.' D3: 'The project is unchanged.'

parts.statement: For PRM-A2's five refused pairings on freshly seeded P, the owner's before and after reads of the title, body, comments and revision list are byte-identical.
For PRM-A3's four no-role requests on freshly seeded P after reading Q, the owner's before and after reads of the title, body, comments and revision list are byte-identical.
Refused and no-role requests preserve the project in other in-scope project states and request histories.

obligations.statement: For each of the four actions, a caller with no role receives the same response as for a nonexistent project, except that Date and X-Request-Id values may differ while retaining the same formats.
obligations.source: D3: 'A caller with no role on the project gets, for each of the four actions, the same response a request for a project that does not exist gets, apart from the values of the Date and X-Request-Id headers, which have the same format as for a project that does not exist.'

parts.statement: PRM-A3's four no-role requests on freshly seeded P after reading Q match the corresponding nonexistent-project status, body and other headers, with matching Date and X-Request-Id formats.
The same response equivalence holds for no-role requests in other in-scope project states and request histories.
